core_claims.claim: Composite DTM 1m is a raster elevation model.
Composite DTM 1m covers about 99 percent of England.
DTM represents terrain after surface-object removal.
DTM production uses bespoke algorithms and manual editing.
Composite DTM uses Time Stamped archive surveys.
Composite DTM also uses National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Repeat-survey selection favours newer and better-resolution data.
Resampled composite data uses bilinear interpolation.
The 2022 composite includes surveys from 2000 through April 2022.
Metadata indexes identify the source survey used at a location.
Composite DTM is available at 2m resolution as a separate product.
A retired 25cm composite was replaced by the 1m composite.
Time Stamped DTM preserves survey-specific archive products.
Time Stamped metadata includes survey date.
Time Stamped metadata includes product resolution.
Time Stamped metadata identifies transformation and geoidal model.
Composite DSM retains surface features unlike DTM.
First-return DSM is a distinct surface product.
Official delivery exposes WMS services for composite products.
Official delivery exposes WCS services for some composite products.
GeoTIFF supports web coverage and image-service delivery.
Point-cloud archives are separate from raster composites.
Exact TQ2892 filtered metadata remains unread in current runtime evidence.
Exact TQ2892 numeric coverage remains unread.
Composite coverage does not identify a candidate parcel boundary.
A DTM value must be bound to an authoritative candidate coordinate.
Survey date and resolution must accompany promoted measurements.
Vertical datum and transformation must accompany promoted measurements.
No value may be inferred from the TQ2892 tile name alone.
Numeric promotion stays blocked without exact service response bytes.
